tools.name: automation_create
tools.title: automation create
tools.description:
Create an automation. Creates an automation on exactly one of canvas or workspace. Instructions come from instructions.

Scheduling is one of three shapes:

cron recurring, on that cadence, interpreted in tz (an IANA zone; the server default applies when omitted)
run_at one-off, a single run at that RFC 3339 instant and no cadence
neither on-demand only: it runs when triggered with automation_run

cron and run_at are mutually exclusive. An invalid cron or time zone is rejected with the server's explanation. Exactly one of: canvas, workspace. At most one of: cron, run_at.

canvas.description: create the automation on this canvas

cron.description: cron cadence for a recurring automation

run_at.description: RFC 3339 instant for a single one-off run (e.g. 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z)

tz.description: IANA time zone the cron fires in (e.g. America/New_York)

workspace.description: create the automation on this workspace

tools.name: automation_delete
tools.title: automation delete
tools.description: Delete an automation. Deletes an automation permanently: its cadence stops and it can no longer be run. Past runs are chats and survive. Deleting an already-deleted automation also succeeds.

tools.name: automation_edit
tools.title: automation edit
tools.description:
Edit an automation. Edits an automation. Only the properties passed are sent; everything else is left unchanged. Setting cron "" clears the cadence entirely, making the automation on-demand only — to stop scheduled runs while keeping the cadence, use automation_pause instead.

run_at schedules a single run at that RFC 3339 instant, which is also how a one-off that has already fired or been paused is re-armed. Setting run_at "" clears the pending run, exactly like pause.

Only the automation's owner can edit it; the server rejects anyone else.

cron.description: new cron cadence ("" clears it, making the automation on-demand only)

run_at.description: RFC 3339 instant for a single one-off run ("" cancels the pending run)

tz.description: new IANA time zone for the cron

tools.name: automation_get
tools.title: automation get
tools.description: Show one automation. Shows one automation in full, including its instructions. The state derives from the stored cadence: active (a next run is scheduled), paused (a cadence is stored but nothing is scheduled), or on demand (no cadence). When the scheduler skipped the most recent firing, the reason and time are shown.

tools.name: automation_list
tools.title: automation list
tools.description: List automations. Lists automations. With no filter, lists the signed-in account's own automations across every canvas and workspace. With canvas or workspace, lists every owner's automations on that one resource (ones the account does not own are read-only). At most one of: canvas, workspace.

canvas.description: list every owner's automations on this canvas

workspace.description: list every owner's automations on this workspace

tools.name: automation_pause
tools.title: automation pause
tools.description:
Pause an automation's scheduled runs. Pauses an automation: the pending run is cancelled while the cron cadence stays stored, so automation_resume picks the schedule back up without re-entering it.

On a one-off (a run-at instant, no cron cadence) there is nothing to resume from: pausing cancels the single pending run outright. Re-arm it with automation_edit run_at.

tools.name: automation_resume
tools.title: automation resume
tools.description:
Resume a paused automation. Resumes a paused automation by re-submitting its stored cron cadence, which makes the platform compute the next run time.

Resuming needs a cadence to recompute from, so it does not apply to a one-off or an on-demand automation — schedule those with automation_edit run_at or automation_edit cron.

tools.name: automation_run
tools.title: automation run
tools.description:
Run an automation now. Starts a run immediately, outside any cadence. The run executes asynchronously in a new chat (flow session) — the session id comes back right away, without waiting for the run to finish.

The scheduler's fire-time gates still apply: an archived or missing target canvas or workspace rejects the run, which exits 1 (error) with the platform's explanation; a billing denial exits 6 (payment required).

tools.name: automation_runs
tools.title: automation runs
tools.description: List an automation's runs. Lists an automation's runs, newest first — scheduled firings and automation_run triggers alike. Each run is a chat (flow session); read one in full with chat_get. Page with before using the previous page's pagination next_ts. Owner-only.

before.description: cursor: the previous page's pagination next_ts

tools.name: canvas_archive
tools.title: canvas archive
tools.description: Move a canvas to the trash. Archives a canvas (soft delete), cascading to the chats and files that live on it. Everything is restorable with canvas_restore — nothing is destroyed.

tools.name: canvas_capture
tools.title: canvas capture
tools.description:
Render a canvas to a webp image. It lets an agent see the canvas as drawn: check layout, overlaps, or how an edit came out. To show a canvas to a person, use canvas_view.

The whole canvas is fit to the frame by default. To see a region as a person would, pass bounds (a rectangle in canvas coordinates, "x,y,width,height") or node_ids; both take the coordinates and ids that canvas_view returns.

The image carries the canvas ground and grid. background solid drops the grid; background transparent drops the ground too, for compositing. The render runs server-side and takes tens of seconds. At most one of: bounds, node_ids. The rendered webp is returned as an image block.

background.description: what sits behind the nodes: grid, solid, or transparent

node_ids.description: frame these nodes. Values containing commas are split

theme.description: theme to render: light or dark

tools.name: canvas_create
tools.title: canvas create
tools.description:
Create an empty canvas in a workspace. Creates a canvas. The workspace is the canvas's home; folder additionally files it into an existing left-rail folder there, by folder ID or by name (matched against the workspace's canvas folders).

Canvases are not files: they live in workspaces and folders, not under file paths. Rename with canvas_rename, relocate with canvas_move, trash with canvas_archive. Put content on it with the canvas_node_add_* tools and canvas_edge_add.

folder.description: file it into this folder (ID or name)

tools.name: canvas_edge_add
tools.title: canvas edge add
tools.description: Add an edge between two nodes. Connects two nodes. source and target are NODE ids from canvas_view — never a file or entity id; for placed files and media the node id differs from the file id, and an edge to a non-node id is skipped. label puts short text at the midpoint ("depends on"). Handles (top-source, right-source, bottom-source, left-source) pin which side the edge leaves and enters; omit them to auto-route, set them for feedback loops and multi-edge pairs.

source_handle.description: pin the source side: top-source, right-source, bottom-source, left-source

tools.name: canvas_edge_delete
tools.title: canvas edge delete
tools.description: Delete edges.

tools.name: canvas_edge_update
tools.title: canvas edge update
tools.description: Update an edge's label or style.

source_handle.description: pin the source side: top-source, right-source, bottom-source, left-source

tools.name: canvas_edit
tools.title: canvas edit

payload.description: The edit payload, sent as a whole object

tools.name: canvas_get
tools.title: canvas get
tools.description: Return one canvas's details. view_url is the public URL to show a person; dashboard_url opens the canvas in the app for a signed-in user.

tools.name: canvas_list
tools.title: canvas list
tools.description: List accessible canvases. Lists every canvas the signed-in account can access, most recently modified first. With workspace, lists only that workspace's canvases (unpaginated — limit does not apply).

limit.description: max canvases to return (server default 25, max 250)

tools.name: canvas_move
tools.title: canvas move
tools.description:
Move a canvas to another workspace or folder. Relocates a canvas in the left rail: workspace re-homes it to another workspace, folder files it into a folder (by ID or name, within its workspace), root moves it back to its workspace's top level. Folder and workspace moves compose: with both, the canvas moves to the workspace first and is then filed into that workspace's folder.

This moves the canvas object only; files ON the canvas stay with it. File records move separately with file_move. At most one of: folder, root.

folder.description: file it into this folder (ID or name)

root.description: move it back to the workspace's top level

workspace.description: re-home the canvas to this workspace

tools.name: canvas_node_add_block
tools.title: canvas node add-block
tools.description:
Create an HTML file and place it as a live block. Creates a text/html file record IN the canvas and places it as a live block — a canvas-native component that renders its HTML at exactly the box it is given. This is the only tool that makes a block; uploading an HTML file and placing it with canvas_node_add_entity yields a plain file card instead.

A block renders at exactly width x height (multiples of 16, minimum 128 per side), so author the HTML to fill that box.

The HTML comes from content. Change its content later through the file id (the file_* tools) — the block re-renders on its own; move or resize through the node id.

chromeless.description: no card chrome: the HTML composites directly onto the canvas

tools.name: canvas_node_add_connector
tools.title: canvas node add-connector
tools.description:
Add a free-floating connector line between two points. Adds a connector: a line or arrow between two absolute canvas coordinates, attached to nothing. To connect two NODES so the link follows them, use canvas_edge_add instead — connectors are for freehand arrows and diagram lines between positions.

Connectors take no position or size; their geometry is start and end. arrow_mode none|end|both presets the arrowheads; curve smooth, straight, or step (default, right-angle).

id.description: node id (UUID v4); omit to auto-generate

tools.name: canvas_node_add_document
tools.title: canvas node add-document
tools.description:
Create an HTML or markdown file and place it as a page card. Creates a file record IN the canvas — text/html or markdown, decided by the destination name's extension — and places it as a standard page card that opens in the detail view. For an HTML component that should render live in a fixed box, use canvas_node_add_block instead.

Cards default to the portrait page (320x416); explicit width/height override it, which is how a deck-style HTML document goes landscape.

tools.name: canvas_node_add_entity
tools.title: canvas node add-entity
tools.description:
Place an entity card: a platform file or a record from another platform. Places an entity card. Two modes:

entity_id places an entity the platform already knows by its data id — this is how a file record is placed on a canvas as a card (pass the file record's ID; for a file from another workspace, add it to this canvas first with file_reference).

platform with id places a generic card describing a record that lives on another platform (slack, notion, github, ...). Nothing is fetched from that platform: the card is built from the fields passed, and the id is stored VERBATIM so repeat placements deduplicate.

entity_id.description: place a known platform entity by data id (a file record's id places the file)

id.description: the record's stable id on that platform, copied verbatim: it labels the card and deduplicates repeat placements, and is never fetched. The node this places gets an id of its own — read that back from canvas_view before drawing edges to it

image_url.description: genuine preview or cover image (renders as a media tile; not for avatars)

platform.description: name of the platform the record lives on (slack, notion, github, ...); it labels the card, and no request is made to that platform

tools.name: canvas_node_add_label
tools.title: canvas node add-label
tools.description:
Add a text label (a single line of free-standing text). Adds a text label: one line of text directly on the canvas — headings, captions, annotations. Font sizes are 16px, 20px (default), 32px, 48px; keep content to roughly 8 words at 16-20px, 5 at 32px, 3 at 48px; a label auto-sizes to its text.

Omit color for the theme-adaptive default (this is usually right). Colors are the spectrum palette: orange, yellow, green, blue, violet, mulberry, brown, indigo, olive.

color.description: spectrum color; omit for the theme-adaptive default

font.description: font family (the same four as canvas_node_add_note)

id.description: node id (UUID v4); omit to auto-generate

tools.name: canvas_node_add_note
tools.title: canvas node add-note
tools.description:
Add a text note (a sticky with a title and markdown body). Adds a text note: a titled sticky holding markdown content. Notes default to 288x288; use 192 height for short notes and 384 for long ones. The title should be 2-6 words.

Colors are the sticky palette: apricot, butter (default), meadow, sea, orchid, rose, clay, mist, oat.

font.description: font family: "Inter, sans-serif", "Georgia, serif", "'Courier New', monospace", "'Comic Sans MS', cursive"

id.description: node id (UUID v4); omit to auto-generate — set it only to reference the node in the same batch

tools.name: canvas_node_add_shape
tools.title: canvas node add-shape
tools.description:
Add a shape (rectangle, circle, diamond, triangle, pentagon, cylinder). Adds a shape, optionally with centered label text (content). Shapes default to 144x144; 192x96 works well for sequence-diagram boxes.

fill takes the sticky palette (apricot, butter, meadow, sea, orchid, rose, clay, mist, oat); stroke takes the spectrum palette and defaults to the stroke paired with the fill. no_fill draws a stroke-only outline.

id.description: node id (UUID v4); omit to auto-generate

shape.description: rectangle, circle, diamond, triangle, pentagon, or cylinder (required)

stroke.description: spectrum stroke color (defaults to the fill's pair)

tools.name: canvas_node_delete
tools.title: canvas node delete
tools.description: Delete nodes from a canvas. Deletes nodes by node id. Deleting a file's node removes the card from the canvas; whether the file itself survives follows the platform's file rules (a reference's deletion removes only the reference).

tools.name: canvas_node_get
tools.title: canvas node get
tools.description:
Read nodes in full. Fetches the complete stored content of specific nodes — the full text of notes that canvas_view truncates, complete entity data, exact geometry.

If a node's content shows it is a file record (entity base "file_record"), the node holds only file METADATA: the file's content is a different id and a different tool — read it with file_read file_record_id (metadata with file_get file_record_id). Passing a file id here fails and says so.

tools.name: canvas_node_move
tools.title: canvas node move
tools.description: Move a node to a new position. Repositions one node by its node id (top-left corner, canvas coordinates, 16px lattice). Works for every node type, including files and media. Content is untouched.

tools.name: canvas_node_resize
tools.title: canvas node resize
tools.description: Resize a node. Resizes one node by its node id (dimensions in canvas units, 16px lattice). position moves it in the same call.

tools.name: canvas_node_update
tools.title: canvas node update
tools.description:
Update a node's content or style. Updates a canvas-native node in place: pass only the properties to change; the rest of the node is untouched (the platform merges partially). The node's current type decides which properties apply — title/content/color for notes and labels, fill/stroke/shape/content for shapes, start/end and the stroke properties for connectors.

Only canvas-native nodes (notes, labels, shapes, connectors) update this way. A file's content is edited through the file itself, and an HTML block through the file_* tools on its file id — the canvas card re-renders on its own.

color.description: note sticky color, label/connector spectrum color

curve.description: connector curve: smooth, straight, or step

tools.name: canvas_publish
tools.title: canvas publish
tools.description:
Publish a canvas to a public URL. Publishes a canvas as a read-only public snapshot — anyone with the URL can view it, no Cohesive account needed. The URL comes back as view_url and is the one to give a person; dashboard_url opens the canvas in the app for a signed-in user. Revoke with canvas_unpublish.

Publishing runs server-side and takes a while (it rebuilds the snapshot and the social card), so this waits for it to finish and reports the outcome. The snapshot is a point-in-time copy: later canvas edits are not published until the canvas is published again. view_url is the public URL to show a person; dashboard_url opens the canvas in the app for a signed-in user.

tools.name: canvas_raw
tools.title: canvas raw
tools.description:
Return a canvas's full content document. Returns the canvas's full content document as {nodes, edges}, each keyed by id. Node and edge shapes follow the canvas frontend's document model and are not a stable contract.

Full documents can be very large — survey with canvas_view first, then use node_ids here to fetch specific nodes in full.

node_ids.description: restrict to these node IDs (and edges between them). Values containing commas are split

tools.name: canvas_rename
tools.title: canvas rename
tools.description: Rename a canvas.

tools.name: canvas_restore
tools.title: canvas restore
tools.description: Restore an archived canvas.

tools.name: canvas_unpublish
tools.title: canvas unpublish
tools.description: Revoke a canvas's public URL. Takes a published canvas offline: the public URL stops serving, and a publish still in flight is cancelled. The canvas itself is untouched.

tools.name: canvas_view
tools.title: canvas view
tools.description: Show a canvas inline. Hosts that support MCP Apps render an interactive board in the conversation; the result is also the canvas's compact projection — identity, geometry, and semantic content with styling stripped and free text truncated — as node and edge tables. Use canvas_raw node_ids to fetch specific nodes in full.

node_ids.description: restrict to these node IDs (and edges between them). Values containing commas are split

tools.name: chat_get
tools.title: chat get
tools.description: Show one chat.

tools.name: chat_list
tools.title: chat list
tools.description: List the signed-in account's chats. Lists the signed-in account's live (non-archived) chats, newest first. Page with before using the previous page's pagination next_ts.

before.description: cursor: the previous page's pagination next_ts

status.description: restrict to statuses (initialized, ready, processing, closed); repeatable. Values containing commas are split

tools.name: file_copy
tools.title: file copy
tools.description: Copy a file record to a new parent or path. Copies a file record to a new destination; the source is untouched. The path rule matches upload. overwrite replaces the contents of an existing record at the destination path, preserving its ID and share state. Exactly one of: workspace, canvas, chat.

overwrite.description: replace the contents of an existing record at the destination path

path.description: destination file path inside Cohesive, e.g. "reports/q3.md" — not a URL and not an API path; without an extension (or with a trailing /) the current file name is kept

tools.name: file_delete
tools.title: file delete
tools.description: Delete a file record. Soft-deletes a file record. Recently deleted records can be restored with file_recover.

tools.name: file_get
tools.title: file get
tools.description: Show one file record. view_url is the URL to show a person; raw_url serves the bytes for fetching or embedding and is not for people; dashboard_url opens the record in the app for a signed-in user. download_url is a signed link to the bytes, valid until download_url_expires_at: the way to move a file anywhere, or to read one file_read cannot return inline.

tools.name: file_list
tools.title: file list
tools.description: List file records under one parent resource, recent files, or deleted files. Lists file records scoped to exactly one parent — a workspace, a canvas, or a chat (flow session) — or one of two cross-workspace views (newest first; page with before): recent, the signed-in account's recently modified Library files, and deleted, recently deleted files still restorable with file_recover. Exactly one of: workspace, canvas, chat, recent, deleted. view_url is the URL to show a person; raw_url serves the bytes for fetching or embedding and is not for people; dashboard_url opens the record in the app for a signed-in user.

before.description: cursor for recent/deleted: the previous page's pagination next_ts

chat.description: list a chat's (flow session's) file records

deleted.description: list recently deleted files (restorable for 14 days)

limit.description: page size for recent/deleted (server default 20, max 100)

recent.description: list the signed-in account's recently modified Library files

tools.name: file_mkdir
tools.title: file mkdir
tools.description:
Create an empty file-system directory. Creates a folder-kind file record — a file-system directory — under exactly one parent: a workspace, a canvas, or a chat (flow session). Directories normally come into being when a file path names them; mkdir exists so an empty directory can be prepared before files move in. Organizing files into folders is this plus file_move path.

Not to be confused with the left-rail folders that organize canvases and chats themselves — those are a separate concept, and these directories only ever group file records. Exactly one of: workspace, canvas, chat.

canvas.description: create the directory in a canvas

chat.description: create the directory in a chat (flow session)

path.description: directory path to create inside Cohesive, e.g. "reports/2026" — not a URL and not an API path

workspace.description: create the directory in a workspace

tools.name: file_move
tools.title: file move
tools.description: Move a file record to a new parent or path. Moves a file record to a new destination. The path rule matches upload: no extension or a trailing / means a directory (the current file name is kept); an extensioned path renames. Omitting path keeps the name at the destination root. Exactly one of: workspace, canvas, chat.

path.description: destination file path inside Cohesive, e.g. "reports/q3.md" — not a URL and not an API path; without an extension (or with a trailing /) the current file name is kept

tools.name: file_promote
tools.title: file promote
tools.description:
Move a canvas or chat file into the workspace Library. Moves a canvas or chat file into the workspace Library — what dragging it to the Library does in the app. The file keeps its ID, and a reference (a link record) is left behind in its source container in the same action, so the canvas or chat still shows the file, now pointing at its Library home.

workspace defaults to the source container's workspace, and parent_path places the file under a Library directory (default: the Library root).

parent_path.description: Library directory to place the file under (default: the root)

workspace.description: Library workspace (default: the source container's workspace)

tools.name: file_publish
tools.title: file publish
tools.description: Publish a file record to a public URL. Makes a file record publicly readable — anyone with the URL can view it, no Cohesive account needed. Two URLs come back. view_url is the viewer page: the one to give a person. raw_url serves the file's bytes: use it to fetch the content, embed the file in another file, or hand it to another service — never as the URL to show someone. Revoke with file_unpublish. view_url is the URL to show a person; raw_url serves the bytes for fetching or embedding and is not for people; dashboard_url opens the record in the app for a signed-in user.

tools.name: file_read
tools.title: file read
tools.description: Read a file record's content. Returns a file record's bytes. For reading, not transfer: text comes back inline up to the output cap and an image up to 3 MiB as an image block; anything else is refused. To move a file anywhere, or read one that does not fit, use file_get and hand its download_url to whatever needs the bytes.

tools.name: file_recover
tools.title: file recover
tools.description: Restore a recently deleted file record.

tools.name: file_reference
tools.title: file reference
tools.description:
Place a reference to a file on a canvas or in a chat. Creates a reference to a file: the reference is its own file record (kind "link") living in the canvas or chat and pointing at the workspace file. The file itself does not move — this is how a Library file, including one from another workspace, is placed onto a canvas without copying it. Copy instead (file_copy) only when a separate file with a separate history is wanted.

Referencing the same file in the same container twice is a no-op; the result says whether the reference already existed. Exactly one of: canvas, chat.

canvas.description: reference the file on a canvas

chat.description: reference the file in a chat (flow session)

tools.name: file_references
tools.title: file references
tools.description: List the references pointing at a file. Lists the link records that reference this file from canvases and chats. The listing is filtered to the containers the signed-in account can view.

tools.name: file_unpublish
tools.title: file unpublish
tools.description: Revoke a file record's public URL.

tools.name: file_upload
tools.title: file upload
tools.description:
Upload a file to a workspace, canvas, or chat. Uploads a file record under exactly one parent: a workspace, a canvas, or a chat (flow session). Pass the file's text as content, or a public URL as from_url for the server to fetch and store the bytes.

path is the destination and names the file exactly, extension included; a directory path has no file name to complete it here. It is required with content, and with from_url it can be omitted to let the server name the file from the URL.

Processing (previews, text extraction, summary) continues server-side after upload; wait blocks until the record reaches status "processed". Exactly one of: workspace, canvas, chat. Exactly one of: content, from_url. There is no base64 property: never encode file bytes into a call.

content.description: the file's text, when authoring it; for existing bytes use from_url

from_url.description: fetch the bytes server-side from a URL and store them: any public URL, including another service's presigned or signed download URL

overwrite.description: replace the contents of an existing record at the destination path

path.description: destination file path inside Cohesive, e.g. "reports/q3.md" — not a URL and not an API path; it names the file exactly, extension included. Required with content; with from_url it can be omitted to let the server name the file from the URL

tools.name: notify_user
tools.title: notify
tools.description:
Send a real in-app notification to the signed-in account. Sends a notification to the signed-in account — it lands in the notification bell in the Cohesive app, exactly like a platform agent's notification. Use it to flag that long-running work finished, that something needs a human decision, or to leave a marker a person will actually see.

The title is the headline (keep it short); body carries the detail. If notifications are not enabled for the organization the call fails saying so rather than silently doing nothing.

tools.name: org_list
tools.title: org list
tools.description: List the signed-in account's organizations.

tools.name: search
tools.title: search
tools.description: Search everything the signed-in account can access. Searches names, file paths, and AI summaries across workspaces, canvases, chats, and files, grouped by resource type.

type.description: restrict to resource types (workspace, canvas, chat, file); repeatable. Values containing commas are split

tools.name: server_info
tools.title: info
tools.description: Show the signed-in user and organization this server acts as, plus its version, the API URL it talks to, mounted and available toolsets, and the tool count. Call it first when unsure whose account the tools run under.

tools.name: tool_help
tools.title: help
tools.description: Return the full help for one tool, e.g. "canvas_node_add_note", for a family of them, e.g. "canvas_node_*", or "" for an overview of this server's whole surface. Use it to learn the arguments and rules behind a tool's description, which is trimmed to a budget.

tool.description: the tool to describe, e.g. "canvas_node_add_note", or a family, e.g. "canvas_node_*", for the tools under it; omit or "" for an overview of the whole surface

tools.name: workspace_get
tools.title: workspace get
tools.description: Show one workspace.

tools.name: workspace_list
tools.title: workspace list
tools.description: List accessible workspaces.
